## File truncation test

credit_record.csv has 1,048,575 data rows, exactly
Excel's limit of 1,048,575. The file is sorted by ID and its final client is
the largest credit ID.
402,053 application IDs lie above that ID and 0 of
them have any credit record, while 36,457 of the
36,457 application IDs at or below it do. The data therefore look cut at the
row limit, and the 'application-only' clients are almost entirely an artefact of that cut, not
applicants who never received a card. The final client has 30 records starting at
relative month -29, and its earliest record is
already C (paid off); a first record of C occurs for
only 0.9% of clients. Result: test **fired**;
the final client is excluded from every analysis table
(1 client).

## Left-truncation test

The earliest vintage (relative month -60) has 231 accounts
against a median vintage of 694, and 99.6% of them
are in 1-29 DPD at MOB 0. The share not in 1-29 DPD at MOB 0 is 0.76% in the first
three vintages and 3.98% in later ones. There is no pile-up and no mature mix, so
the test **did not fire** and no vintage is excluded.

## New charge-offs within 12 months (event counts)

| Origin month | Open in status 0-4 | Reaching status 5 within 12M | Pilot | Agrees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| -36 | 5954 | 29 | 29 | yes |
| -30 | 6770 | 34 | 34 | yes |
| -24 | 7674 | 34 | 32 | differs |
| -18 | 8664 | 37 | 35 | differs |
| -12 | 9554 | 41 | 41 | yes |

Origins where this build differs from the pilot: -24 (34 vs pilot 32), -18 (37 vs pilot 35). This build counts an account when any status-5 month occurs in the 12 months after the origin; the brief does not state its counting rule, so the small gap is recorded rather than forced. These small counts drive the design of the backtest (count calibration, small-n flags).
